mismatches_summary.pattern: same bias as Gemini: treats a resolved/stale past worry as an UNDERSTANDING increment that 'earns' the current relief
same bias as Gemini: treats an unresolved material change as still usable to enrich understanding

different failure mode: correctly rejects the candidate but picks the wrong negative bucket (NOT_SUITABLE instead of SEMANTIC_ABSTAIN) -- a boundary-line miss, not an over-eager UNDERSTANDING invention

conclusion: Swapping to a genuinely independent challenger model family (Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 vs the Google Gemini 2.5 Flash family used in every prior round) produced a real, decisive improvement (+2 exact matches, 9/12 vs 7/12), confirming part of the prior bias was model-family-specific. But 2 of the 3 remaining Claude Haiku mismatches reproduce the identical systematic error Gemini made: treating a stale/unresolved past item as a permissible UNDERSTANDING increment. This is no longer explainable purely as 'wrong challenger model' -- it recurs across two independent model families on the same construct, which points at the review construct/rubric itself still leaving room for this specific error, not (only) at model choice.
recommendation: Before spending more on challenger-model search, tighten the suitability construct/rubric specifically against the STALE_RESOLVED_OR_CONFLICTING and MATERIAL_CHANGE_UNRESOLVED failure patterns (both mismatches independently reproduced across Gemini and Claude), then re-test with the same 12-item anchor set before considering the larger 201-item pass.
